market_summary: Pre-market snapshot as of 07:10 IST (latest sourced pre-open update): GIFT Nifty was quoted at 25,304.50, below Tuesday's Nifty close of 25,387.40, indicating a cautious opening bias; this is an indicative futures quote, not the cash opening print. On 17 Nov, Nifty 50 closed at 25,387.40 (+0.38%) and Sensex at 82,532.19 (+0.52%), both at their highest levels since late February. Banks and private banks reached record highs; small-caps fell 0.2% while mid-caps rose about 0.3%. Overnight, Wall Street's technology-led decline was followed by a recovery in Asian equities after Nvidia's better-than-expected sales forecast; Brent was around $93/bbl. The rupee settled at 93.47 per US dollar on Tuesday, supported by foreign equity inflows and lower oil. NSE provisional cash data showed FII net buying of ₹4,195.38 crore and DII net buying of ₹196.93 crore on 17 Nov. For the accessible portfolio, HDFC Bank disclosed a routine employee stock-option/RSU grant; no newly verified material issuer-specific development was found in this scan for HUL, ITC, SJVN, Tata Steel, SBI Cards, Manappuram Finance, Vodafone Idea or the recorded funds/ETFs. Verified facts are separated from interpretation below; no directional outcome is assured.

global_cues.title: Asian equities rebounded after Nvidia's sales outlook
global_cues.detail: Reuters reported MSCI Asia-Pacific ex-Japan up 0.9%, South Korea's KOSPI up as much as 3.3%, Japan's Nikkei up 0.6% and S&P 500 e-mini futures up 0.5% in early Wednesday trade. Nvidia rose 4.7% after hours following quarterly revenue above forecasts. The regional rebound followed four losing sessions, but market breadth and individual country moves varied.

global_cues.title: Wall Street fell for a fourth consecutive session before Nvidia's report
global_cues.detail: Reuters said the S&P 500 fell 1% on Tuesday, its fourth straight daily decline, before Nvidia reported. The subsequent after-hours Nvidia move improved sentiment toward AI hardware suppliers, but does not erase the preceding risk-off session.

global_cues.title: Anthropic IPO pricing is another AI sentiment test
global_cues.detail: Reuters reported that Anthropic was due to price its shares later on Wednesday ahead of a market debut that could value the company at up to $1.4 trillion. The pricing and investor response may influence sentiment toward high-valuation AI businesses; the valuation is a reported potential figure, not a completed market capitalisation.

global_cues.title: Dollar and US Treasury yields remain firm
global_cues.detail: Reuters reported the US dollar index at 103.66 and the US 10-year Treasury yield at 5.123%. A St. Louis Fed official said several rate hikes may be needed to bring inflation under control. A firm dollar and elevated yields can remain headwinds for emerging-market currencies and valuation-sensitive equities.

global_cues.title: Oil held near $93 amid supply and shipping risks
global_cues.detail: Brent was around $93 per barrel in early Asian trade, down about 0.2% in Reuters' snapshot. Traders weighed a projected supply surplus and recovering Middle East exports against continued tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and US crude inventory expectations.

investing.headline: HDFC Bank grants 1,86,031 stock options and 41,377 restricted stock units under employee schemes
investing.what_changed: The bank's NSE-filed disclosure dated 17 Nov says its Governance, Nomination and Remuneration Committee granted 1,86,031 equity stock options under ESOS Plan H-2024 and 41,377 restricted stock units under its Employees' Stock Incentive Master Scheme 2022. The filing sets out a staged vesting schedule over 48 months.
investing.why_it_matters: This is a routine employee-retention and incentive action for a recorded portfolio holding, rather than a new operating or earnings catalyst. The long vesting schedule spreads potential equity issuance over time.
investing.risk: The eventual share impact depends on vesting and exercise conditions; this grant alone does not indicate a change in asset quality, earnings, deposit growth or loan demand.
investing.source: HDFC Bank NSE filing – grant of stock options and restricted stock units, 17 Nov 2026

macro.name: Nifty 50 / Sensex – 17 Nov close
macro.context: Both benchmarks closed at their highest levels since late February. They were up about 10.1% and 10.8%, respectively, month to date according to Reuters.

macro.name: Sector and broader-market performance
macro.value: Banks +1.1%; private banks +0.9%; financials +0.6%; PSU banks +2.0%; small-caps -0.2%; mid-caps +0.3%
macro.context: 17 Nov close. Eleven of 16 major sectors advanced; banks and private banks reached record highs. This indicates leadership from financials alongside weaker small-cap breadth.

macro.name: GIFT Nifty
macro.context: Moneycontrol's 07:10 IST pre-market update said the futures indication was lower than Tuesday's Nifty cash close of 25,387.40, suggesting a cautious start. This is an indicative futures quote, not the NSE opening level.

macro.name: FII / DII cash-market flows
macro.value: FII net buying ₹4,195.38 crore; DII net buying ₹196.93 crore
macro.context: 17 Nov 2026, NSE provisional cash-market data. Combined net buying was ₹4,392.31 crore. Provisional figures may be revised; FII cash buying does not by itself describe derivatives positioning.

macro.name: USD/INR
macro.value: Rupee settled at 93.47 per US dollar on 17 Nov
macro.context: Reuters reported the rupee at a more than seven-month high, up about 1.5% this month. Foreign equity inflows and a more favourable oil-price environment were cited as supports; RBI intervention remains a factor to watch.

macro.name: Brent crude
macro.value: Around $93 per barrel in early Asian trade
macro.context: Reuters' 18 Nov snapshot showed Brent down about 0.2%. Supply-surplus expectations and recovering exports are counterbalanced by shipping-security concerns around the Strait of Hormuz. Lower crude is generally supportive for India's import bill, all else equal.

macro.name: US dollar index / US 10-year Treasury yield
macro.context: Reuters early Wednesday snapshot. Firm dollar and elevated Treasury yields may tighten global financial conditions and weigh on emerging-market currency and equity valuations.
